label: MY STORY
heading: Journey
intro: I did not follow a conventional path into technology. Starting late taught me how to catch up, begin again, and make what I learn useful to other people.

chapters.label: Starting late
chapters.title: Formal school began when I was eleven.
chapters.summary: I entered class two much older than everyone around me, with years of education to rebuild and a persistent feeling that I was already behind.
chapters.fullText: I was born in 1997 in Pakistan, and my early years were spent entirely on Islamic studies. I did not begin formal school until I was eleven. Starting in class two, much older than everyone around me, made every gap feel visible. I moved through only odd-numbered classes while rebuilding the foundation other students already had.

chapters.label: Catching up
chapters.title: Effort became the advantage I could control.
chapters.summary: Computer Science was another difficult beginning, so I rebuilt the basics through long days of self-study until the work finally started to click.
chapters.fullText: Getting into a good Computer Science university did not remove the self-doubt. I struggled with concepts that seemed familiar to everyone else and decided to compensate with consistency. Some days meant eighteen hours of teaching myself, practising code, and rebuilding the basics from the ground up. By my third year, that effort began to turn into confidence and real opportunities.

chapters.label: Giving back
chapters.title: Progress felt more meaningful when it helped someone else.
chapters.summary: Internships led to professional work, while mentoring, nonprofit leadership, workshops, and writing gave that growth a wider purpose.
chapters.fullText: My first internship quickly led to professional roles, but work was only part of the story. I began leading a nonprofit, mentoring students, and eventually became a chairman. Helping thousands of students find their way was one of the most rewarding parts of my early career. After graduating, I continued through workshops and writing for people from non-traditional backgrounds.

chapters.label: Starting again
chapters.title: Moving to Berlin created another reset.
chapters.summary: A new country, language, and professional environment brought back the discomfort of starting over—and the confidence that I could do it again.
chapters.fullText: In 2022, I moved to Germany. Starting over in a new country and language was difficult, but it was also a fresh beginning. I worked to find my place in Berlin and eventually joined Mercedes-Benz.io, where I now contribute to digital products used by customers around the world.

chapters.label: Building and sharing
chapters.title: Today, the work and the teaching belong together.
chapters.summary: I build digital products, explore applied AI, and turn what works into practical talks, workshops, mentoring, and writing.
chapters.fullText: Today, I work at the intersection of building software and helping people. I write and speak about engineering, careers, and relocation because I want others to see that a late or difficult start does not define the finish. My journey has been full of resets and long nights, and it continues to shape how I build, learn, and share.
